title: Project Harrier Planning
provenance: Synthetic transcript authored for this repository; no real meeting content.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Welcome everyone to the Project Harrier planning session. Let's review where we are.

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: Thanks Carlos. I've completed the initial risk assessment and identified three major technical challenges.

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: Can you walk us through those Diana?

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: Sure. First challenge is the database migration from MySQL to Postgres. Second is API backwards compatibility. Third is the caching layer redesign.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Those sound significant. What's your confidence level on the migration timeline?

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: I'd say seventy percent confident we can finish by March twentieth if we start next week.

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: What happens if we slip?

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: If we slip past March twentieth, we risk missing the Q2 launch window entirely.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Okay, so the migration is our critical path. Elena, where are we on the frontend redesign?

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: Frontend is progressing well. We've completed the component library and started on the dashboard views.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Any blockers?

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: Not blockers, but we need final design approval from the product team by next Friday.

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: I can coordinate with product to expedite that. Should I set up a review meeting?

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: Yes please, that would be really helpful.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Great. Moving on to budget - I reviewed the cloud infrastructure costs and we're tracking about fifteen percent over budget.

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: Is that the Aurora instance?

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Partly. The Aurora instance is ten thousand dollars per month but we also have increased data transfer fees.

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: Can we optimize that before the migration?

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: We should. I'll ask the DevOps team to audit our data transfer patterns.

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: Good idea. Also, did we get approval for the two additional contractors?

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Not yet. Still waiting on finance. I'll follow up with Sarah tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: We really need those contractors by February tenth at the latest.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Agreed. I'll make it clear that's a hard deadline.

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: What about testing? Do we have enough QA capacity?

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: That's actually another concern. Our QA team is already stretched thin.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Could we bring in a QA contractor as well?

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: Makes sense. I'll include that in the budget request.

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: For the API backwards compatibility issue, I think we need to maintain two versions for at least six months.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: That adds complexity though.

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: It does, but it's safer than breaking existing integrations. We have about forty clients on the current API.

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: Exactly. We can't afford to break them.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Fair point. Let's plan for dual API versioning then. Diana, can you document the version strategy?

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: Will do. I'll have a draft by end of week.

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: One more thing - security audit. When is that scheduled?

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Good question. I think it's scheduled for late February but I need to confirm.

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: We should do it before the migration, not after.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Agreed. I'll reach out to the security team today.

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: Are we tracking all these action items somewhere?

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Yes, I'll update the project board after this meeting with everything we discussed.

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: Perfect. Anything else on the technical roadmap?

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: Just a heads up that the monitoring dashboard redesign is on hold until we complete the main migration.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Makes sense. We don't want to distract from the critical path.

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: Should we schedule our next check-in?

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Yes, let's do two weeks from today, same time.

segments.speaker: Elena Rodriguez
segments.text: Works for me.

segments.speaker: Diana Chen
segments.text: Same here. I'll send calendar invites.

segments.speaker: Carlos Mendes
segments.text: Great. Thanks everyone for a productive session. Let's keep the momentum going.
